findings.failure_scenario: The new provenance paragraph cites its own file by LINE NUMBER: 'are stated here because line 43 of this file demands exactly that'. Verified against the staged bytes: line 43 is indeed '- Whether a result was MEASURED or inferred', so the citation resolves TODAY. It is the only line-number self-citation in any file under .agents/skills/ or docs/internal/standards/ (grep over both trees returns this one hit). The '## Never cut' list it points into spans lines 34-46 and grew by that very bullet during round 2, so it is an actively growing list; adding one bullet above line 43 silently repoints the citation at 'The reason behind a recommendation'. Nothing catches it: check-rule-citations.sh refuses numeric citations only of review.md's rules (STANDARD=docs/internal/standards/review.md, NAMES derived from that file), and check-links.sh resolves link targets, not line offsets. This repository landed that gate ONE COMMIT AGO, 69b4f13 'M0.72: name the review rules, because a number names nothing and goes stale', whose body records that a citation had already drifted unnoticed ('a citation of a 12b, which resolves to no rule at all'). This commit reintroduces the identical defect one level out, inside the file whose job is to tell agents what not to cut. Fix is to cite the clause by its text -- 'the Never-cut clause on MEASURED or inferred' -- which costs the same tokens and cannot go stale.
findings.remedy: Replace 'line 43 of this file' with the clause's name, e.g. 'the Never-cut clause on whether a result was MEASURED or inferred'.

findings.failure_scenario: The provenance paragraph is internally contradictory and is placed where the reader it is written for does not reach it. (a) CONTRADICTION: lines 82-84 read 'They hold on BPE vocabularies of the common family and not universally -- "auth" is one token where "authentication" is several, so that abbreviation does save tokens.' The em-dash clause is offered as the illustration of 'not universally', but auth/authentication is a counterexample ON the common BPE family, not off it. So the sentence asserts the claims hold on family X and then refutes one of them on family X in the same breath. The refuted claim is line 52-53, 'The tokenizer splits them the same as the full word: zero tokens saved', which remains stated flat as fact. An agent that loads this skill, reads '## Never fake-compress', and quotes 'zero tokens saved' downstream propagates an unmeasured claim the file itself has already contradicted -- the non-negotiable-4 failure the packet's documentation lens names, unchanged from F7 for that reader. (b) PLACEMENT: the claims are at lines 52-57 under '## Never fake-compress'; the correction is at 81-85, twenty-four lines and two intervening headings later ('## Scale length to the task', '## Write at full length when'), and 'THE TOKENIZER CLAIMS ABOVE' names no section. Under this skill's own rules an agent reads the section it needs and stops. The provenance now EXISTS in the file, which is why this is minor rather than the major it would be if it did not; what it does not do is reach the point of use. The clean fix is the one F7 offered as its second option: delete the three token-arithmetic justifications from lines 53, 55 and 57 and let the three rules stand on readability, which lines 84-85 already concede is what they stand on. That removes the contradiction, removes the unmeasured claim, removes the need for the paragraph, and shortens the file.
findings.remedy: Delete the token-arithmetic clauses at lines 53, 55, 57 and the paragraph at 81-85; keep the three rules on readability grounds. If the paragraph is kept instead, move it directly under line 50 and drop the self-refuting 'They hold on BPE vocabularies of the common family' sentence.
